front: What does the sales ledger hold?
back: The personal accounts of credit customers (trade receivables). ZIMSEC: trade receivables (debtors') ledger.

front: What does the purchases ledger hold?
back: The personal accounts of credit suppliers (trade payables). ZIMSEC: trade payables (creditors') ledger.

front: What does the nominal (general) ledger hold?
back: All other accounts: sales, purchases, returns, income, expenses, non-current assets, inventory, capital, drawings, loans.
In the nominal (general) ledger, not in the sales ledger.
Division of work; better control and less fraud; easier location of errors; quick information on receivables and payables.

front: Why is the cash book part of the double entry?
back: Its cash and bank columns are the cash and bank accounts, so only the other side of each entry is posted.

front: Posting the purchases journal to a divided ledger
back: Each invoice: credit the supplier (purchases ledger). Total: debit purchases (nominal ledger).
Software keeps customer, supplier and general ledger modules; one entry posts both sides and balances update at once. Back up and password-protect the data.
